steps.question: What separates groups on the page?
steps.why: Strong borders separate groups at any zoom.

steps.question: Which color roles does it need?
steps.why: Few color roles, each with one clear meaning.

steps.pick: neutral.0: the base for content; body text reads 18.42:1 on it, above the 7:1 floor.
steps.darkPick: neutral.100: We use the step above the page for content in dark in order to leave a darker step free for wells, as the gray's two darkest steps are too close to tell apart. The fill does this by moving content one step up: sunken reads 1.16:1 below it and raised 1.26:1 above it. So people tell wells and menus from content, and body text still reads 14.85:1, because dark ships as standard (theming.values), text keeps the AAA floor (accessibility.definition) and depth reads from tone and lines (elevation.definition).

steps.pick: neutral.900: the strongest text step, 18.42:1 on surface.default, above the 7:1 floor.
steps.darkPick: neutral.900: the strongest text step, 14.85:1 on surface.default, above the 7:1 floor.

steps.question: What is the smallest target?
steps.why: Large targets for tremor and touch.

steps.question: How large is body text?
steps.why: Large text is readable for more people.
Large targets help people with motor needs.
Clear rectangles read as fields and buttons.

steps.pick: radius.6: We use the 6px control corner for boxes that grow in order to keep their role, as objects of one family, by inheritance from the control corner. The same radius does this by giving a text area or a list row the curve of the fields beside it. So people see one family of boxes on a form, because the control corner is slight, not a pill (shape.values), and the brand is clear (brand.q1).

steps.question: How many signals carry each meaning?

steps.why: Selection never relies on color alone.

steps.rule: The fill of a selected or current item, or a toggle that is on.
steps.pick: blue.light.100: a tint of the brand, 1.18:1 from content, always beside its edge (border.selected), so selection is never color alone.
steps.darkPick: blue.dark.100: a tint of the brand, 1.04:1 from content, always beside its edge (border.selected), so selection is never color alone.

steps.rule: The edge that marks a selected item, beside its fill, so selection is never color alone.
steps.pick: blue.light.600: the edge beside a selected fill, so selection is never color alone, 7.26:1 on surface.default, above the 3:1 floor.
steps.darkPick: blue.dark.600: the edge beside a selected fill, so selection is never color alone, 7.55:1 on surface.default, above the 3:1 floor.

steps.question: Which states get their own visible value?
steps.why: Every state, including loading, gets its own value.
Moderate speed is easy to follow.

steps.rule: The fill of the item the pointer or the keyboard is on, or whose submenu is open. A state shows on the item's background, one step from the surfaces it sits on: darker in light, and darker in dark too, as raised layers take the lighter step.
steps.pick: neutral.100, two steps darker than the surfaces it sits on (neutral.0), so the item under the pointer or the keyboard reads as a band without lifting off the page. It skips neutral.50, the page canvas, so a menu item never matches the page behind it.
steps.darkPick: neutral.50: We use a step darker than content for the item under the pointer or the keyboard in dark, in order to mark it as a band on both surfaces it meets: 1.16:1 on surface.default and 1.46:1 on surface.raised. The fill does this by stepping darker, as raised layers took the lighter step; muted text still reads 8.89:1 on it. So the hovered row or menu item shows on cards and menus alike, because hover and focus have their own look (accessibility.roles) and the neutral ramp sets the steps (color.definition).

steps.rule: The fill of an item while it is pressed. Where the scheme gives pressed its own value, one step past the highlight; where pressed reuses hover, the highlight's step.
steps.pick: neutral.200, one step past the highlight (neutral.100), so a press reads as its own change under the finger: every state, including loading, gets its own value.
steps.darkPick: neutral.200: We use the raised layer's step for a pressed sidebar item in dark in order to show a press as a change of its own, apart from the hover band and from the page. The fill does this by stepping lighter while the hover band steps darker: 1.46:1 from the highlight, 1.26:1 from content and 1.57:1 from the canvas, which keeps the darkest step. A pressed item never sits on a raised layer, so sharing that step hides nothing. So a press reads under the finger, because every state, loading included, gets its own value (accessibility.roles) and the neutral ramp sets the steps (color.definition).

steps.question: What contrast floor do we hold?

steps.use: button/focus-ring at focus.ring.width, with an offset
steps.why: Focus must be seen by everyone.

steps.pick: blue.light.600: the focus ring, so the keyboard's place is never lost, 7.26:1 on surface.default, above the 3:1 floor.
steps.darkPick: blue.dark.700: We use the brand blue one step above its key for the focus ring in dark in order to hold the ring at 7:1 where focus moves through menus and dialogs. The ring does this by reading 9.33:1 on surface.default and 7.41:1 on surface.raised, where the key step (blue.dark.600) gave 6.0:1 on the raised layer. So keyboard users never lose their place inside a dialog, because the focus ring keeps the AAA level on every surface (accessibility.definition) and the brand ramp sets its hue (color.definition).
